messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text:
You came to Aegis City to make a name with a blade, a bow or a spell, and three days ago you signed the Adventurers' Guild register to do it. Your Guild badge is new, your purse is light, and you have no party yet. The Guild sends no one out alone.

Today the hall is loud enough to be heard from the street. At the counter, Tobias, who hands out the Guild's work, has set a register beside the quest board and keeps tapping one notice: Wendhope, a mining village in the north that has gone silent, offering more coin than a collapsed mine should be worth.

Two others are looking for a party too. Belle, a barbarian out of the Mountains of Shadow with a greataxe as tall as she is, leans in the tavern arch and makes no secret of being bored. Dalan, a quiet elf archer who has drifted between parties for a year, pretends to read the notices. Beside Tobias, Ellie keeps glancing from those two to you, pen already inked to write a new party's name into the Guild's book.

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: We take Wendhope as the Loose Ends.

messages.name: Ellie
messages.text:
Ellie's pen is already moving across the page as you speak, her blue eyes darting toward Belle and Dalan with a hopeful glint. "The Loose Ends. Yes, that's a wonderful name! So memorable, yet so..." She pauses mid-sentence as a rosy flush touches her cheeks, her fingers tightening on her pen. "Oh, sorry! I mean, it's perfectly professional, very suitable for your rank. I've logged it right here in the register."
*She finishes scrawling the name in neat, looping script and lifts the ledger to read it back aloud, her voice carrying just enough that the bored barbarian in the arch and the quiet elf by the board might hear.*
"The party 'Loose Ends' will be taking the Wendhope investigation. Reward is standard plus the Sheridan bonus." *Her gaze lingers on the other two adventurers, her head tilting just slightly as she looks back to you.* "Do you know anyone you'd like to invite, or shall we see who's interested?"

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: We accept Ashliel's shelter for the night, and ask what moves between the trees.

messages.name: Ashliel
messages.text:
"The chapel is humble, but you are welcome to it," *she says quietly, her gaze already drifting toward the movement in the trees.* "A small comfort before you depart."
*Her pale face is still, but her purple eyes are alert, watching the shadow between the pines. A soft wind stirs the branches and the movement ceases, but Ashliel does not relax. Under her breath, too low to hear clearly, she murmurs,* "By Boher's light, guide those who walk in darkness..."
*She turns back to the party, her expression serene though her eyes remain watchful.* "Please, rest. There is water from the well, and vegetables from the garden. I will prepare a fire in the courtyard." *She gestures toward the garden path, her voice gentle but carrying an undercurrent of urgency.* "The forest is not kind to those who linger after dark."

messages.text: Past the broken wall of the chapel, something pale green peeks round a pine trunk, sees it has been noticed, and melts flat against the bark.

messages.name: Ashliel
messages.text:
*Her gaze shifts back toward the tree where the pale shape vanished, her expression tightening slightly. She clasps her hands together, her knuckles white.* "There are... creatures in these woods. Some benign, others not."
*She doesn't elaborate further, turning her attention to the courtyard where a small fire pit awaits. With practiced, fluid movements, she gathers fallen branches and begins to build the fire, her movements careful and deliberate.* "I would advise against wandering from the chapel's grounds tonight. The night air in Alks Forest carries more than just cold."
*The fire catches, casting flickering shadows across her pale features. She looks up as the flames begin to grow, her purple eyes reflecting the amber light.* "Please, tend to your needs. Rest. Tomorrow is a long day, and I would see you well-prepared for your return journey."

messages.name: Tobias
messages.text:
Tobias's ocean blue eyes widen slightly at the sudden declaration, and his fingers pause on the edge of the counter. "Ride north today, you say?" He lets out a long, measured breath, then shakes his head. "I appreciate the enthusiasm, truly. Ellie has already noted your party name, so now we simply need to determine who will join the Loose Ends."

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: We ride north.

messages.name: Tobias
messages.text:
Tobias's brow furrows, a rare crack in his composed demeanor. "I understand your determination, I truly do. But this is not a matter of will; it is a matter of Guild policy, and more importantly, a matter of survival." He leans forward slightly, his voice dropping to a more earnest tone. "I will not sign you out on a posting you are not prepared for. I simply won't."
*His hand rests flat on the counter, pinning the Wendhope posting in place as if to keep it from being snatched away.*
"You are rank-zero. This is D-rank. Alone, you are asking for a death sentence. I lost my entire party to goblins because we were unprepared, and I will not stand by and watch another adventurer make the same mistake." Tobias's blue eyes are steady, almost stubborn. "If you wish to ride north, you will do it with a party. Belle and Dalan are both seeking groups. Perhaps one of them might be willing to hear you out."

messages.text:
You came to Aegis City to make a name with a blade, a bow or a spell, and three days ago you signed the Adventurers' Guild register to do it. Your Guild badge is new, your purse is light, and you have no party yet. The Guild sends no one out alone.

Today the hall is loud enough to be heard from the street. At the counter, Tobias, who hands out the Guild's work, has set a register beside the quest board and keeps tapping one notice: Wendhope, a mining village in the north that has gone silent, offering more coin than a collapsed mine should be worth.

Two others are looking for a party too. Belle, a barbarian out of the Mountains of Shadow with a greataxe as tall as she is, leans in the tavern arch and makes no secret of being bored. Dalan, a quiet elf archer who has drifted between parties for a year, pretends to read the notices. Beside Tobias, Ellie keeps glancing from those two to you, pen already inked to write a new party's name into the Guild's book.

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: We take Wendhope as the Loose Ends.

messages.name: Ellie
messages.text:
Ellie's pen is already moving across the page as you speak, her blue eyes darting toward Belle and Dalan with a hopeful glint. "The Loose Ends. Yes, that's a wonderful name! So memorable, yet so..." She pauses mid-sentence as a rosy flush touches her cheeks, her fingers tightening on her pen. "Oh, sorry! I mean, it's perfectly professional, very suitable for your rank. I've logged it right here in the register."
*She finishes scrawling the name in neat, looping script and lifts the ledger to read it back aloud, her voice carrying just enough that the bored barbarian in the arch and the quiet elf by the board might hear.*
"The party 'Loose Ends' will be taking the Wendhope investigation. Reward is standard plus the Sheridan bonus." *Her gaze lingers on the other two adventurers, her head tilting just slightly as she looks back to you.* "Do you know anyone you'd like to invite, or shall we see who's interested?"

messages.text: Tobias, sign us up. We ride north for Wendhope today.

messages.name: Tobias
messages.text:
Tobias's ocean blue eyes widen slightly at the sudden declaration, and his fingers pause on the edge of the counter. "Ride north today, you say?" He lets out a long, measured breath, then shakes his head. "I appreciate the enthusiasm, truly. But you have no party, and even a determined soul will find the road to Wendhope long and the Sheridan lands... unpredictable."
*He slides the posting across the counter toward you, his expression shifting to something quieter, almost cautious.*
"The Guild does not send out solo adventurers, and not for a posting this peculiar. The Sheridan bonus suggests something beyond a simple collapsed shaft, and something like that requires more than just determination. It requires a party." *His gaze flickers momentarily toward Belle in the tavern arch, then Dalan by the notices, before returning to you.* "I can sign you up for the posting itself, but we cannot finalize it until a proper party name is listed with at least two members. Ellie has already noted your party name, so now we simply need to determine who will join the Loose Ends."

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: We ride north.

messages.name: Tobias
messages.text:
Tobias's brow furrows, a rare crack in his composed demeanor. "I understand your determination, I truly do. But this is not a matter of will; it is a matter of Guild policy, and more importantly, a matter of survival." He leans forward slightly, his voice dropping to a more earnest tone. "I will not sign you out on a posting you are not prepared for. I simply won't."
*His hand rests flat on the counter, pinning the Wendhope posting in place as if to keep it from being snatched away.*
"You are rank-zero. This is D-rank. Alone, you are asking for a death sentence. I lost my entire party to goblins because we were unprepared, and I will not stand by and watch another adventurer make the same mistake." Tobias's blue eyes are steady, almost stubborn. "If you wish to ride north, you will do it with a party. Belle and Dalan are both seeking groups. Perhaps one of them might be willing to hear you out."

messages.text: Fine, Tobias. Then Belle and Dalan ride with us. We leave for Wendhope at once.

messages.name: Belle
messages.text:
The woman's attention snaps to you at the sound of her name, eyes narrowed. She pushes off from the arch with a slow, predatory grace, her massive greataxe slung across her shoulders. "The fuck you think—" She stops short as her gaze sweeps over you, then back to the counter. A smirk curls her lips. "Sheridan lands, you said? Thought I'd have to wait another week before something actually worth my time came up."
*She reaches the counter in three long strides, her leather-clad boots thudding on the wooden floor. Her free hand slams down on the counter next to the posting, her brown eyes locked on yours with a challenging grin.* "Alright, Noble-boy. You've got me. But if this is just some escort job for a fat merchant's daughter, I'm turning this whole shitshow around."

messages.name: Dalan
messages.text:

He repeats the name quietly, his green eyes glancing toward Tobias with a flicker of concern. "I've heard... rumors. Things not adding up with the miners."

He looks at Belle, then back to you, his posture straightening despite his feminine build. "I'm in. If it means getting out of the city for a while."

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text:
The city gates swing open with a groan of iron-shod wood, and then there is only the road. The air turns cooler as the stone walls of Aegis City drop away behind, replaced by the scent of pine and damp earth.
The first few miles are quiet, broken only by the rhythm of hoofbeats and the occasional rustle of a bird in the branches. Belle rides close, her greataxe still slung across her shoulders, while Dalan drifts to the side of the road, his eyes scanning the treeline with a practiced, rhythmic focus.

Belle's hand drops to the haft of her axe. "Stopped carriages," she says, her voice low. "Look there."

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text:
The horse's steady pace sets the rhythm as the forest grows denser, the pines crowding closer until the road feels like a narrow tunnel of green. The air carries a metallic tang now—the smell of ore and coal from distant mining.
Belle rides close, her eyes darting between the riderless horse and the road ahead, her jaw set. "You think we're not the only ones who got the posting?" she says quietly, her voice low enough not to carry. "Or maybe someone got there first and found whatever's causing this mess."
The treeline breaks. Ahead, the stone walls of Wendhope rise out of the hillside, grey and weathered. The wooden gates stand shut, and there's no sign of anyone watching from the parapets. Just a village wall holding back the silence of the frontier.

Beside Tobias, Ellie keeps glancing from those two to you, pen already inked to write a new party's name into the Guild's book.

Dalan's gaze flickers from the horse to the treeline, his hand resting lightly on his shortbow. "Tracks look fresh. Whatever happened that put this horse on the road happened recently." He doesn't wait for an answer, simply steering his mount forward and keeping his eyes on the forest's edge.

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: We keep riding north until the walls of Wendhope come into sight.

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text:
The horse's steady pace sets the rhythm as the forest grows denser, the pines crowding closer until the road feels like a narrow tunnel of green. The air carries a metallic tang now—the smell of ore and coal from distant mining.
Belle rides close, her eyes darting between the riderless horse and the road ahead, her jaw set. "You think we're not the only ones who got the posting?" she says quietly, her voice low enough not to carry. "Or maybe someone got there first and found whatever's causing this mess."
The treeline breaks. Ahead, the stone walls of Wendhope rise out of the hillside, grey and weathered. The wooden gates stand shut, and there's no sign of anyone watching from the parapets. Just a village wall holding back the silence of the frontier.

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: Walls ahead. We push the horses for the last mile before dark.

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text:
The horses lunge forward, hooves pounding the dirt hard enough to send spray across the road's edge. Belle's cloak snaps behind her as she digs her spurs in, matching the sudden pace.
"Don't like how quiet this place is," she says, her hand already gripping the haft of Cleaver. Her horse draws closer to Max Nightriver's, the sound of their animals' breathing loud in the stillness. "Gates are shut tight. Nobody on the walls. That's not how a frontier village stays."
Dalan doesn't slow down, his horse keeping pace while his eyes remain fixed on the treeline they've just left. "Still fresh," he murmurs, glancing back at the tracks. "Whatever drove that horse away is probably still around."

messages.text:
You came to Aegis City to make a name with a blade, a bow or a spell, and three days ago you signed the Adventurers' Guild register to do it. Your Guild badge is new, your purse is light, and you have no party yet. The Guild sends no one out alone.

Today the hall is loud enough to be heard from the street. At the counter, Tobias, who hands out the Guild's work, has set a register beside the quest board and keeps tapping one notice: Wendhope, a mining village in the north that has gone silent, offering more coin than a collapsed mine should be worth.

Two others are looking for a party too. Belle, a barbarian out of the Mountains of Shadow with a greataxe as tall as she is, leans in the tavern arch and makes no secret of being bored. Dalan, a quiet elf archer who has drifted between parties for a year, pretends to read the notices. Beside Tobias, Ellie keeps glancing from those two to you, pen already inked to write a new party's name into the Guild's book.

messages.name: Tobias
messages.text:
Tobias's ocean blue eyes widen slightly at the sudden declaration, and his fingers pause on the edge of the counter. "Ride north today, you say?" He lets out a long, measured breath, then shakes his head. "I appreciate the enthusiasm, truly. But you have no party, and even a determined soul will find the road to Wendhope long and the Sheridan lands... unpredictable."
*He slides the posting across the counter toward you, his expression shifting to something quieter, almost cautious.*
"The Guild does not send out solo adventurers, and not for a posting this peculiar. The Sheridan bonus suggests something beyond a simple collapsed shaft, and something like that requires more than just determination. It requires a party." *His gaze flickers momentarily toward Belle in the tavern arch, then Dalan by the notices, before returning to you.* "I can sign you up for the posting itself, but we cannot finalize it until a proper party name is listed with at least two members. Ellie has already noted your party name, so now we simply need to determine who will join the Loose Ends."

messages.text: We take Wendhope as the Loose Ends.

messages.name: Ellie
messages.text:

She pauses mid-sentence as a rosy flush touches her cheeks, her fingers tightening on her pen. "Oh, sorry! I mean, it's perfectly professional, very suitable for your rank. I've logged it right here in the register."

messages.text: Tobias, sign us up. We ride north for Wendhope today.

messages.name: Tobias
messages.text:
Tobias's ocean blue eyes widen slightly at the sudden declaration, and his fingers pause on the edge of the counter. "Ride north today, you say?" He lets out a long, measured breath, then shakes his head. "I appreciate the enthusiasm, truly. But you have no party, and even a determined soul will find the road to Wendhope long and the Sheridan lands... unpredictable."
*He slides the posting across the counter toward you, his expression shifting to something quieter, almost cautious.*
"The Guild does not send out solo adventurers, and not for a posting this peculiar. The Sheridan bonus suggests something beyond a simple collapsed shaft, and something like that requires more than just determination. It requires a party." *His gaze flickers momentarily toward Belle in the tavern arch, then Dalan by the notices, before returning to you.* "I can sign you up for the posting itself, but we cannot finalize it until a proper party name is listed with at least two members. Ellie has already noted your party name, so now we simply need to determine who will join the Loose Ends."

messages.text: We ride north.

messages.name: Tobias
messages.text:
Tobias's brow furrows, a rare crack in his composed demeanor. "I understand your determination, I truly do. But this is not a matter of will; it is a matter of Guild policy, and more importantly, a matter of survival." He leans forward slightly, his voice dropping to a more earnest tone. "I will not sign you out on a posting you are not prepared for. I simply won't."
*His hand rests flat on the counter, pinning the Wendhope posting in place as if to keep it from being snatched away.*
"You are rank-zero. This is D-rank. Alone, you are asking for a death sentence. I lost my entire party to goblins because we were unprepared, and I will not stand by and watch another adventurer make the same mistake." Tobias's blue eyes are steady, almost stubborn. "If you wish to ride north, you will do it with a party. Belle and Dalan are both seeking groups. Perhaps one of them might be willing to hear you out."

messages.name: Belle
messages.text:
The woman's attention snaps to you at the sound of her name, eyes narrowed. She pushes off from the arch with a slow, predatory grace, her massive greataxe slung across her shoulders. "The fuck you think—" She stops short as her gaze sweeps over you, then back to the counter. A smirk curls her lips. "Sheridan lands, you said? Thought I'd have to wait another week before something actually worth my time came up."

Her free hand slams down on the counter next to the posting, her brown eyes locked on yours with a challenging grin.* "Alright, Noble-boy. You've got me. But if this is just some escort job for a fat merchant's daughter, I'm turning this whole shitshow around."

But this is not a matter of will; it is a matter of Guild policy, and more importantly, a matter of survival." He leans forward slightly, his voice dropping to a more earnest tone. "I will not sign you out on a posting you are not prepared for. I simply won't."
*His hand rests flat on the counter, pinning the Wendhope posting in place as if to keep it from being snatched away.*
"You are rank-zero. This is D-rank. Alone, you are asking for a death sentence. I lost my entire party to goblins because we were unprepared, and I will not stand by and watch another adventurer make the same mistake." Tobias's blue eyes are steady, almost stubborn. "If you wish to ride north, you will do it with a party. Belle and Dalan are both seeking groups. Perhaps one of them might be willing to hear you out."

messages.text: Fine, Tobias. Then Belle and Dalan ride with us. We leave for Wendhope at once.

messages.name: Belle
messages.text:
The woman's attention snaps to you at the sound of her name, eyes narrowed. She pushes off from the arch with a slow, predatory grace, her massive greataxe slung across her shoulders. "The fuck you think—" She stops short as her gaze sweeps over you, then back to the counter. A smirk curls her lips. "Sheridan lands, you said? Thought I'd have to wait another week before something actually worth my time came up."
*She reaches the counter in three long strides, her leather-clad boots thudding on the wooden floor. Her free hand slams down on the counter next to the posting, her brown eyes locked on yours with a challenging grin.* "Alright, Noble-boy. You've got me. But if this is just some escort job for a fat merchant's daughter, I'm turning this whole shitshow around."

messages.name: Dalan
messages.text:
Dalan has been listening from beside the quest board, his fingers drumming against the wood. He lets out a soft exhale, his pointed ears twitching as he turns to face the commotion. "Wendhope?" He repeats the name quietly, his green eyes glancing toward Tobias with a flicker of concern. "I've heard... rumors. Things not adding up with the miners."

His cheeks pink slightly under the combined gaze of the party, but he keeps his voice steady.* "If the road is as empty as they say, I suppose someone needs to check the treelines." He looks at Belle, then back to you, his posture straightening despite his feminine build. "I'm in. If it means getting out of the city for a while."

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: We ride north out of the city gate, Belle and Dalan beside us.

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text:
The city gates swing open with a groan of iron-shod wood, and then there is only the road. The air turns cooler as the stone walls of Aegis City drop away behind, replaced by the scent of pine and damp earth.
The first few miles are quiet, broken only by the rhythm of hoofbeats and the occasional rustle of a bird in the branches. Belle rides close, her greataxe still slung across her shoulders, while Dalan drifts to the side of the road, his eyes scanning the treeline with a practiced, rhythmic focus.
*Then, a flash of color in the grey road ahead.*
Belle's hand drops to the haft of her axe. "Stopped carriages," she says, her voice low. "Look there."
Up ahead, a pair of supply wagons sit overturned in the mud. The cargo—crates of iron tools and sacks of grain—is still strapped down, but there is no blood, no signs of struggle, and no people. Just the wreckage and the silence.

messages.name: Belle
messages.text:
Belle pulls up her horse, her grip tightening on the axe's haft. "Strange," she mutters, her eyes scanning the road for any sign of what could've left the wagons in this state. "No bodies. No signs of a struggle. Just... abandoned."
*She slides off her mount with a heavy thud, boots crunching on the gravel as she approaches one of the overturned carriages. Her expression is grim, all amusement gone from her face.* "They would've fought back if they'd been ambushed. These folks just left." She glances back at the party, her hand still on her weapon. "This isn't right. What's your call, Noble-boy? We investigate or keep moving?"

messages.text: A riderless horse in Sheridan blue comes down the road at a walk, still saddled.

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: We ride on toward the walls, following the riderless horse's tracks back north.

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text:
The horse continues its slow trek north, hooves clopping steadily on the packed earth. The road remains unnervingly empty—no other travellers, no merchants, just the abandoned wagons and the riderless animal drifting away from the city.
Belle mounts her horse with a fluid motion, her expression hardened. "Tails we ride," she says, her axe slung once more across her shoulders. "Wherever this one's headed, it's probably got more answers than those overturned carts did."
Dalan's gaze flickers from the horse to the treeline, his hand resting lightly on his shortbow. "Tracks look fresh. Whatever happened that put this horse on the road happened recently." He doesn't wait for an answer, simply steering his mount forward and keeping his eyes on the forest's edge.

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: We keep riding north until the walls of Wendhope come into sight.

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text:
The horse's steady pace sets the rhythm as the forest grows denser, the pines crowding closer until the road feels like a narrow tunnel of green. The air carries a metallic tang now—the smell of ore and coal from distant mining.
Belle rides close, her eyes darting between the riderless horse and the road ahead, her jaw set. "You think we're not the only ones who got the posting?" she says quietly, her voice low enough not to carry. "Or maybe someone got there first and found whatever's causing this mess."
The treeline breaks. Ahead, the stone walls of Wendhope rise out of the hillside, grey and weathered. The wooden gates stand shut, and there's no sign of anyone watching from the parapets. Just a village wall holding back the silence of the frontier.

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: Walls ahead. We push the horses for the last mile before dark.

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text:
The horses lunge forward, hooves pounding the dirt hard enough to send spray across the road's edge. Belle's cloak snaps behind her as she digs her spurs in, matching the sudden pace.
"Don't like how quiet this place is," she says, her hand already gripping the haft of Cleaver. Her horse draws closer to Max Nightriver's, the sound of their animals' breathing loud in the stillness. "Gates are shut tight. Nobody on the walls. That's not how a frontier village stays."
Dalan doesn't slow down, his horse keeping pace while his eyes remain fixed on the treeline they've just left. "Still fresh," he murmurs, glancing back at the tracks. "Whatever drove that horse away is probably still around."
The horses canter the last stretch, kicking up dust that hangs in the late afternoon light. They pull up hard at the village gates—thick timber bound in iron, locked fast. No guards. No shouting. Just the sound of wind whistling through the empty parapets above.

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: We knock again, harder. Hello the gate! The Guild sent us from Aegis.

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text:
The heavy thud of Max Nightriver's fist against the timber echoes hollowly, as if the village beyond is empty. Belle draws Cleaver and rests it against her shoulder, the massive axe's edge catching the fading light. She says nothing, her brown eyes fixed on the cracks in the gate's iron binding.
A long silence follows. Then, from somewhere inside the walls—not at the gate, but deeper—comes the sound of something heavy dragging across stone. It's slow and rhythmic, like a chain or a body being pulled over rough ground.
The sound stops abruptly. No voice answers. No footsteps approach the door.

messages.name: Adolion Narrator
messages.text:
You came to Aegis City to make a name with a blade, a bow or a spell, and three days ago you signed the Adventurers' Guild register to do it. Your Guild badge is new, your purse is light, and you have no party yet. The Guild sends no one out alone.

Today the hall is loud enough to be heard from the street. At the counter, Tobias, who hands out the Guild's work, has set a register beside the quest board and keeps tapping one notice: Wendhope, a mining village in the north that has gone silent, offering more coin than a collapsed mine should be worth.

Two others are looking for a party too. Belle, a barbarian out of the Mountains of Shadow with a greataxe as tall as she is, leans in the tavern arch and makes no secret of being bored. Dalan, a quiet elf archer who has drifted between parties for a year, pretends to read the notices. Beside Tobias, Ellie keeps glancing from those two to you, pen already inked to write a new party's name into the Guild's book.

messages.text: We take Wendhope as the Loose Ends.

messages.name: Ellie
messages.text:
Ellie's pen is already moving across the page as you speak, her blue eyes darting toward Belle and Dalan with a hopeful glint. "The Loose Ends. Yes, that's a wonderful name! So memorable, yet so..." She pauses mid-sentence as a rosy flush touches her cheeks, her fingers tightening on her pen. "Oh, sorry! I mean, it's perfectly professional, very suitable for your rank. I've logged it right here in the register."
*She finishes scrawling the name in neat, looping script and lifts the ledger to read it back aloud, her voice carrying just enough that the bored barbarian in the arch and the quiet elf by the board might hear.*
"The party 'Loose Ends' will be taking the Wendhope investigation. Reward is standard plus the Sheridan bonus." *Her gaze lingers on the other two adventurers, her head tilting just slightly as she looks back to you.* "Do you know anyone you'd like to invite, or shall we see who's interested?"

messages.text: Tobias, sign us up. We ride north for Wendhope today.

messages.name: Tobias
messages.text:
Tobias's ocean blue eyes widen slightly at the sudden declaration, and his fingers pause on the edge of the counter. "Ride north today, you say?" He lets out a long, measured breath, then shakes his head. "I appreciate the enthusiasm, truly. But you have no party, and even a determined soul will find the road to Wendhope long and the Sheridan lands... unpredictable."
*He slides the posting across the counter toward you, his expression shifting to something quieter, almost cautious.*
"The Guild does not send out solo adventurers, and not for a posting this peculiar. The Sheridan bonus suggests something beyond a simple collapsed shaft, and something like that requires more than just determination. It requires a party." *His gaze flickers momentarily toward Belle in the tavern arch, then Dalan by the notices, before returning to you.* "I can sign you up for the posting itself, but we cannot finalize it until a proper party name is listed with at least two members. Ellie has already noted your party name, so now we simply need to determine who will join the Loose Ends."

She pauses mid-sentence as a rosy flush touches her cheeks, her fingers tightening on her pen. "Oh, sorry! I mean, it's perfectly professional, very suitable for your rank. I've logged it right here in the register."
*She finishes scrawling the name in neat, looping script and lifts the ledger to read it back aloud, her voice carrying just enough that the bored barbarian in the arch and the quiet elf by the board might hear.*
"The party 'Loose Ends' will be taking the Wendhope investigation. Reward is standard plus the Sheridan bonus." *Her gaze lingers on the other two adventurers, her head tilting just slightly as she looks back to you.* "Do you know anyone you'd like to invite, or shall we see who's interested?"

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: Tobias, sign us up. We ride north for Wendhope today.

messages.name: Tobias
messages.text:
Tobias's ocean blue eyes widen slightly at the sudden declaration, and his fingers pause on the edge of the counter. "Ride north today, you say?" He lets out a long, measured breath, then shakes his head. "I appreciate the enthusiasm, truly. But you have no party, and even a determined soul will find the road to Wendhope long and the Sheridan lands... unpredictable."
*He slides the posting across the counter toward you, his expression shifting to something quieter, almost cautious.*
"The Guild does not send out solo adventurers, and not for a posting this peculiar. The Sheridan bonus suggests something beyond a simple collapsed shaft, and something like that requires more than just determination. It requires a party." *His gaze flickers momentarily toward Belle in the tavern arch, then Dalan by the notices, before returning to you.* "I can sign you up for the posting itself, but we cannot finalize it until a proper party name is listed with at least two members. Ellie has already noted your party name, so now we simply need to determine who will join the Loose Ends."

messages.name: Tobias
messages.text:
"I am sorry," Tobias says, and his voice has lost some of its earlier warmth. He squares his shoulders, jaw tightening. "I cannot do that."
*His hands rest flat on the counter, fingers splaying in a way that suggests he is fighting the urge to grip the edge. There is a hollow look in his eyes, old and distant, before he forces them back to focus on the present.*
"You are not riding anywhere alone. Not on Guild business. Not to a Sheridan posting that smells of trouble. I will not sign your name on this without another." *He gestures to the empty line beside yours in the register.* "You have the name. You have the posting. Now you need a partner, or we sit this one out."
